plugin.name: Build Apple Apps
plugin.description: Bring the iOS Simulator into the activity panel: the agent builds, installs, launches and drives the app on screen, with a built-in SwiftUI guide covering both patterns and diagnosis.
tab.label: Simulator
gate.unsupported.title: macOS only
gate.unsupported.body: The iOS Simulator relies on Xcode and CoreSimulator, so it runs on macOS only.
gate.missing.title: baguette is not installed
gate.missing.body: Screen mirroring and gesture injection are provided by baguette (Apache-2.0). Run the command below in a terminal, then choose Re-check.
gate.outdated.title: baguette is out of date
gate.outdated.body: Found {{found}}, but this plugin needs {{required}} or newer. iOS 26 changed the gesture-injection calling convention, so older builds silently do nothing. Upgrade, then choose Re-check.

settings.runtime.outdated: Found baguette {{found}}, but {{required}} or newer is required. iOS 26 changed the gesture-injection calling convention, so older builds silently do nothing.

settings.service.heading: Simulator service
settings.options.heading: Panel options
settings.options.alwaysShowTab.title: Always show the simulator tab
settings.options.alwaysShowTab.descripti: By default the tab appears only in directories recognised as an Xcode or SwiftPM project. Turn this on when the project is not at the repository root.
settings.options.autoStartServer.title: Start the service when the panel opens
settings.options.autoStartServer.descrip: When off, start it manually from the panel — useful if you would rather not keep a background process running.
settings.subtitle: Runtime status, service control and panel options
settings.tagline: Drive an iOS Simulator right in the activity panel — screen, taps, logs and device tools in one place, on the same device the agent uses.
settings.runtime.installHint: Run the command below in a terminal to install or upgrade, then choose Re-check:
settings.service.hint: The plugin starts the service on a host-allocated port bound to 127.0.0.1, and it is reclaimed when the plugin is disabled or the app quits.
settings.footer.credit: Screen mirroring and gesture injection are provided by baguette (Apache-2.0). This plugin gates the runtime, starts the service and embeds its console in the panel.
settings.footer.agent: On the agent side a built-in Skill locates controls by accessibility label rather than deriving coordinates from screenshots, and pulls in the SwiftUI component, Liquid Glass and performance-audit guides on demand.
panel.noDevice: No simulators available. Create a device in Xcode first.
settings.device.heading: Default device
settings.device.label: Open the panel on
settings.device.hint: Automatic selection reuses an already-booted device first, then prefers iPhone 17 Pro. The panel boots the device for you when it is not running.
